Import PNG files as pdr drawings

Source: R/pdr_import_png.R
pdr_import_png.Rd

Reads PNG files generated by custom software and converts them into pdr_drawing elements (see pdr_match()), so that the rest of the paindrawr pipeline can be used. The pixel data is stored in the .rgba element. Since a PNG holds no stroke information, .points and .strokes are empty tibbles with the expected column types.

Usage

pdr_import_png(
  files,
  background = NULL,
  background_tolerance = 0,
  id_from_filename = TRUE
)

Arguments

files

Character vector of paths to PNG files.

background

Optional colour (anything grDevices::col2rgb() accepts, e.g. "white" or "#000000") that marks the background of PNGs without an alpha channel (1 or 3 channels). Matching pixels get alpha 0; all others get alpha 1. Ignored for PNGs that already have alpha. If NULL (default), such PNGs are fully opaque. Note that drawn pixels of exactly the background colour cannot be distinguished from background.

background_tolerance

Maximum absolute difference (0-1 scale, per channel) from background for a pixel to count as background. Default 0 (exact match). Increase to remove anti-aliasing halos, at the cost of also removing faint strokes.

id_from_filename

Logical. If TRUE (default), .id is the file name without directory and .png extension. If FALSE, .id is NA_character_.

Value

A pdr_tibble (see pdr_match(); as from pdr_import_json()) with one row per file and columns pdr_data (a pdr_list of pdr_drawings, each containing .id, .file, .version, .width, .height, .units, .timestamp, .app, .points, .strokes and .rgba) and id.

Details

PNGs with fewer than four channels are converted to RGBA without loss of information: grayscale (1 channel) is replicated to R, G and B with alpha set to 1; grayscale + alpha (2 channels) is replicated to R, G and B; RGB (3 channels) gets alpha set to 1. Indexed (palette) PNGs are expanded to RGB(A) by png::readPNG(). Pixels that are fully transparent are set to black (rather than transparent white). The row order of .rgba is as returned by png::readPNG() (row 1 is the top of the image).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pdr_tibble <- pdr_import_png(c("drawing_a.png", "drawing_b.png"))
} # }

# Import an example PNG (grayscale/RGB without alpha: opaque unless
# `background` is given)
pdr_import_png(pdr_example_file("bg_full_body.png"))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   pdr_data          id          
#>   <list>            <chr>       
#> 1 <named list [11]> bg_full_body

# Treat white pixels as background (alpha 0)
pdr_import_png(pdr_example_file("bg_full_body.png"), background = "white")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   pdr_data          id          
#>   <list>            <chr>       
#> 1 <named list [11]> bg_full_body
